messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: node nimbus-3: gpu0 experienced CUDA_OOM despite headroom metric passing thresholds. auto-ticket #INC-3055 created. severity: P1-ish until we confirm impact

sara: seeing elevated OOM count on nimbus-3 from ~10:12 UTC, rate ~3/min. headroom gauge shows ~1.2GB free on that GPU at alert time.

jon: interesting — that usually means fragmentation or reserved blocks not available. pulling dmesg + allocator logs now.

jon: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-14T10:12:34Z] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
allocator: reserve_total=6.0GiB headroom=1.2GiB spare_pool=512MiB
kv_cache: active_prefixes=128 reserved_blocks=64 fragment_pct=38
node: nimbus-3 gpu0
```

mike: are we seeing pagefaults or prefetch spikes? paging would make headroom meaningless if resident pages were evicted.

jon: good call. checking syslog: saw repeated pagefault messages around same time — some container reported slow host page-in.

kirti: can someone check reserved-block usage? if reserved blocks are pinned and fragmented we can OOM even with headroom.

jon: query to runtime telemetry:
```sql
SELECT sum(reserved_blocks_in_use), avg(fragmentation), count(prefetch_events)
FROM gpu_telemetry
WHERE node='nimbus-3' AND gpu='gpu0' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes'
```
returned: reserved_in_use=60 / 64, frag=42%, prefetch_events=180

sara: that frag number is high. 60/64 reserved used means no spare blocks to satisfy large contiguous allocs.

ops-bot: NOTE: we've throttled new deployments to nimbus-3 via routing policy.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable prefetch on that node 2) drop non-critical caches (KV prefix eviction) 3) if still failing, gracefully restart affected containers to free pinned blocks. anyone object?

jon: +1 on plan. how to disable prefetch quickly?

kirti: CLI: `redwoodctl node set-attr nimbus-3 --prefetch=false` — that will stop the runtime from issuing new prefetches but won't evict current pinned blocks.

mike: ok run it and also trigger `kvtool evict --node nimbus-3 --policy lru --target 40%` to free cache.

jon: ran both commands at 10:16:12 UTC: prefetch=false returned ok, kv evict started. seeing KV evict progress messages.

sara: after eviction, reserved_in_use dropped to 32/64 and frag -> 28%, OOM events slowed but not fully stopped. some containers still hitting large allocs.

support: FYI a few customer requests to /generate returned 503 between 10:11-10:20 UTC. we have 4 tickets opened (T-9921, T-9922, T-9923, T-9924). letting support know mitigation started.

mike: next step if still flaky: schedule rolling restart for heavy alloc containers on that GPU, but first try graceful heap release pattern. jon, can you patch runtime to attempt deferred-reserve fallback?

jon: can push a hotfix that reduces reserve claim size for new model load requests (force smaller contiguous allocations). will deploy canary to nimbus-1 then roll to nimbus-3 if OK.

ops-bot: Deploy canary job started: runtime-hotfix v2026.03.14-rc1 -> nimbus-1 at 10:25 UTC.

kirti: if hotfix works, we still need to follow up with storage team — page-in latency hints that host memory pressure or kernel swapping had windows. we should correlate with host-level OOM-killer or swap activity.

mike: support update please: what customer impact window and approximate qps affected?

support: initial customers affected: 3 mid-market teams, approx 120 failing reqs, majority retries succeeded after 10-30s. ticket notes updated.

sara: hotfix passed canary (10:30), rolling to nimbus-3 now. watching allocator telemetry.

jon: after hotfix roll (10:35), reserved_in_use down to ~28/64, fragmentation falling to 20%, OOM events rate -> near zero. Containers that were failing recovered, traffic lookback shows errors dropped to baseline.

mike: good. immediate mitigation summary: stopped prefetch, evicted KV prefixes, rolled hotfix to reduce contiguous reserve sizes. avoided node reboot.

kirti: action items postmortem: 1) improve telemetry to alert on reserved_blocks saturation (not just headroom), 2) add an automated fallback to reduce reserve size when fragment_pct > 30% and reserved_in_use > 85%, 3) investigate host page-in windows and tune prefetch backoff.

jon: adding logs + commands we ran to incident ticket for reproduction and dev tests.

sara: handing over to next oncall for follow-up — @mike will transition to next-day oncall at 18:00 UTC. please pick up postmortem ownership.

mike: taking postmortem. I'll coordinate writeup, assign action items, and schedule cross-team sync with storage.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. incident duration ~24m. auto-close timer set for 2h pending regression.

support: updating customers with mitigation summary and ETA for postmortem.

jon: quick note — we should prioritize a telemetry panel: reserved_blocks_in_use, frag_pct, prefetched_pages/sec, and direct mapping to 5xx rates. saved for PM/infra backlog.

sara: thanks everyone. leaving thread for final notes. :white_check_mark:
